Team — quick internal calc after skimming Alice’s workbook. Putting numbers here so we can finalize the brief for the customer tomorrow: 

Assumptions (proposal):
- Launch DAU used for sizing: 15,000 (customer stated).
- Sessions/day: assume 40% of DAU start a session => 6,000 sessions/day.
- Avg turns per session: 3 turns (user + assistant counts as 1 turn each) => 6,000 * 3 = 18,000 turns/day.
- Tokens per turn: prompt 110 + response 260 = 370 tokens/turn.
- Daily tokens ≈ 18,000 * 370 = 6,660,000 tokens/day.
- Monthly (30 days) ≈ 200M tokens/month.

Peak planning: assume a 3x spike from releases — peak day tokens ~20M tokens. P99 latency target for interactive chat customers usually ~800ms for p95, p99 depends on model. For 7B-class models on hosted infra we can commonly hit p95 ~250–350ms and p99 ~500–800ms with proper batching and KV caching; for 70B-variants p99 can be several seconds unless on dedicated low-latency GPUs or quantized kernels.

Model tradeoffs (shortlist phrasing for the customer doc):
- 7B instruction-tuned: cost-efficient, low-latency, good throughput. Recommend for high-volume, modest reasoning.
- 13B chat-tuned (8k): better at multi-turn coherence and doc grounding; reasonable throughput with optimized kernels.
- 70B (quantized / dedicated): best quality for retrieval + complex reasoning across long contexts; higher cost and requires Dedicated / Private for predictable p99.

Operational recommendations for the proposal:
- Start with hosted API on mixed model slate (7B + 13B) and configure smart routing by intent: low-cost model for trivial queries, mid-tier for doc grounding, high-tier for flagged edge cases.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated doc lookups — big reduction in per-token compute.
- Recommend enabling 8k context at launch; include 32k in roadmap once we have telemetry on long-context frequency.

Action items for Marissa/Monica:
- Marissa — include these numbers in the customer brief and call out the monthly token estimate ~200M.
- Monica — will you confirm CS readiness to run a 45-min workshop and capture release-day spike plans?
- Rishi — can you sketch expected p99 latency for each candidate model on hosted vs Dedicated (approx numbers)?

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Alice — following our internal sizing run and Ben’s notes above, here’s a concise package you can share with your engineering/product leads before the workshop. Quick summary first, then the attached brief has model-level latencies and estimated costs.

Shortlist (recommended for evaluation):
- Redwood-Edge-7B-instruct (cost-efficient): low p99 on hosted, best throughput; good default for high-volume Q&A.
- Redwood-Chat-13B-8k (balanced): stronger doc grounding for multi-turn flows with 8k context.
- Redwood-Large-70B-q4 (high quality): quantized 70B for difficult reasoning / long-context tasks; recommend Dedicated for predictable p99.

Sizing summary (launch baseline):
- Sessions/day (assumed): 6,000
- Avg turns/session: 3
- Avg tokens per turn: 370
- Daily tokens: ~6.7M
- Monthly tokens (30d): ~200M
- Peak-day (3x release spike): ~20M tokens

Context recommendation: enable 8k context at launch, include telemetry for long-context usage. If >10% of sessions require >8k we will plan a 32k rollout.

Hosting recommendation: start on Hosted API (mix of 7B + 13B) and route by intent; expand to Dedicated if you require hard p99 SLAs for the 70B path or want data isolation.
